classification.difficultyReason: Apply the vertical line test, with the hardest case requiring excluded open circles and filled replacement points to be interpreted together at each marked input.

inlines.text: Which of the following represent functions?

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 1, left cell; printed question 19.
spec.description: An increasing blue straight line with arrows at both ends crosses the negative x-axis and positive y-axis. Black axes have positive-end arrows and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled nonvertical straight line. No numerical coordinates, ticks, grid or equation are supplied. Internal drawing coordinates encode the source arrangement only.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible. Classification and explanation belong only to the answer fields.

answer.worked: Function. Every vertical line intersects the sloping line exactly once.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 1, right cell; printed question 20.
spec.description: A blue cubic-shaped curve runs from lower left to upper right with arrows at both ends. Its local maximum is left of the y-axis and above the x-axis; its local minimum is right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. It crosses the origin and crosses the x-axis once on each side.
spec.mathematics: An unscaled single-valued curve with two turning points and three x-axis crossings. No equation or numerical values are supplied; the editable curve preserves the depicted topology without assigning a source equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible. No vertical test lines or classifications appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked: Function. Every vertical line meets the curve exactly once; the turning points do not give multiple outputs for one input.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 2, left cell; printed question 21.
spec.description: A blue upward-opening parabola has its vertex at the origin and an arrow at each upper end. Black unscaled axes carry x and y labels and positive-end arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: The vertex is at the axes' intersection and the branches are symmetric about the y-axis. No scale, numerical coefficient or equation is asserted; plotting parameters reproduce the unscaled shape.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied parabola and axes appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked: Function. Every vertical line intersects the upright parabola exactly once.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 2, right cell; printed question 22.
spec.description: A blue sideways parabola opens right from the origin. Its upper and lower branches have arrows at their right-hand ends. Black axes have positive-end arrows and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: The branches are symmetric about the x-axis and share a vertex at the origin. Positive horizontal positions meet both branches. Internal plotting coordinates do not supply a numerical equation or scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied graph appears. Test lines and the classification remain in the answer content.

answer.worked: Not a function. A vertical line to the right of the origin intersects both branches, giving two outputs for one input.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 3, left cell; printed question 23.
spec.description: A complete unfilled blue circle is centred at the axes' intersection. Both black axes extend beyond the circle and have positive-end arrows and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: A circle centred at the origin, without a specified radius, scale, numerical coordinates or curve arrowheads. The internal radius is a drawing parameter only.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete source circle and axes remain visible; no answer marks are added.

answer.worked: Not a function. A vertical line through the circle's centre intersects the upper and lower arcs, giving two outputs for the same input.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 3, right cell; printed question 24.
spec.description: A blue upper semicircular arc extends from the negative x-axis to the positive x-axis. It has no lower arc, endpoint circles or curve arrows. Black axes are labelled x and y.
spec.mathematics: Upper semicircle centred about the origin. No radius, coordinate values or scale are supplied. Every vertical line has at most one intersection with the arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied semicircle and axes are shown; the classification is answer content.

answer.worked: Function. Every vertical line intersects the upper semicircle at most once.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 4, left cell; printed question 25.
spec.description: A blue vertical line to the right of the y-axis crosses the positive x-axis and has arrows at both ends. Black unscaled axes have positive-end arrows and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: The vertical line has a positive but unspecified x-coordinate. No numerical value, ticks or equation are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The vertical relation is a permanent given; its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: Not a function. The single input represented by the vertical line has many outputs, so the graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 4, right cell; printed question 26.
spec.description: A blue horizontal line lies below the x-axis, crosses the negative y-axis and has arrows at both ends. Black axes have positive-end arrows and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: A constant negative output with no specified numerical value. Axes have no ticks, numbers or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied horizontal relation and axes are shown.

answer.worked: Function. Every vertical line intersects the horizontal line exactly once. Different inputs may have the same output.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 5, left cell; printed question 27.
spec.description: Two blue straight rays form an upright V with vertex at the origin and outward arrows at the upper-left and upper-right ends. Black axes have x and y labels and positive-end arrows.
spec.mathematics: Both arms lie above the x-axis and occupy opposite sides of the y-axis. They meet only at the origin. No numerical slope, angle or equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied V is always visible; classification and reasoning remain answer content.

answer.worked: Function. Every vertical line meets the V exactly once, including at the vertex. The two arms occupy opposite sides of the y-axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Left page column, graph array row 5, right cell; printed question 28.
spec.description: A descending blue line passes continuously through the origin and has arrows at both ends. Three hollow blue circles lie in quadrant II and three in quadrant IV. Six filled blue points form an ascending arrangement, three in quadrant III and three in quadrant I. Each filled point shares its horizontal position with one hollow circle.
spec.mathematics: Exactly six open-circle exclusions and six filled replacements, paired by horizontal position. White interiors interrupt the descending line at the excluded points. The origin has neither a hole nor an added point marker. No scale, numerical coordinates, ticks or equation are printed; internal positions are schematic drawing parameters.
spec.answerVisibility: All six hollow markers and six filled markers are permanent supplied givens. No classification, vertical test lines or explanatory labels are added to the question graph.

inlines.text: Open circles are excluded; each has one filled replacement at the same input.

answer.worked: Function. Open circles are excluded. At each of the six marked inputs, exactly one filled replacement point supplies the output. At every other input, the descending line supplies one output, including at the origin. Every vertical line therefore meets the graph exactly once.
